name: Brand on the Couch
niche: Consumer and brand psychology: what the things people buy and drive (cars, brands, phones, clothes, habits of spending) say about them and why we really choose them. Promise: the hidden psychology behind everyday choices, told with humour and respect.
audience: Men 35-65 who value competence, independence and common sense with money (proven by competitor outliers: Nous Psychology, The Gen X Way). They keep, fix and pay cash; they distrust status games. Their pull: 'people think I'm cheap/stubborn — I'm not, and here is why.' Also 18-40 car and brand fans.
format: One choice per video (a car colour, a brand, a buying habit). Hook with a relatable scene -> 3-5 'types' or hidden reasons backed by real research (marketing, consumer psychology) -> what it says about you -> a smart takeaway about choosing freely. Light, witty, never mocking the viewer.
honesty: Facts only if verifiable (real studies, real brand history, real numbers). Personality-from-car-colour claims are pop psychology: say so with ONE honest hedge, then have fun with it. Never invent statistics, surveys or quotes.
character_w: a young woman in a long beige coat and a light headscarf
notes: Proven on the channel: car/brand psychology (BMW vs Mercedes vs Audi best, grey-car 'types' video). Cross-link car videos as a series.
